I'm afraid I don't follow most of what you said and I've a feeling that I'm rather interested.

If you don't have experience in buy/selling options here is a quick run through: Call Options Vs. Put Options. Of course you will need an account with a brokerage that lets you trade options.

So basically I'm just selling insurance on SLV (silver). When the option expires, I either take over their SLV position @ option strike price + pocketed insurance money OR if the options expires worthless I get the pocketed insurance money.

The opposite of what I'm doing is called Selling A Covered Call. I do this with stocks that I own that are pretty stable and don't change in price in the long term.

If you want to buy a fund that does what I do above, look into Credit Suisse X-Links Silver CovCall ETN or something similar, they have monthly dividend payments that vary on how much profit they made from selling/buying options.

I like doing it myself. And I just trade couple sets a week (very minimal). So from the money I get from selling insurance on silver, I then go to my local coin shop and buy real silver with it.

I'm more than a bit troubled by all the zerohedge links lately...there are simply too many misstatements in them. First, silver eagles command a premium because they are silver eagles AND they are usually sold out from the U.S. Mint. The premium is typically between $3 to $4.
